title: Parking service and strategies
idea: The core design is a ParkingLot facade that gates call to park and check out, with spot choice and pricing behind swappable strategy interfaces.

analogy.text: A car park office. Gate staff only phone the office; the office checks its floor chart for a spot and its rate card for the price.
analogy.breaks: Here a new rule is a new class; old ones stay untouched.

points: EntryGate and ExitGate are thin: they call ParkingLot and show the result.
`SpotAllocationStrategy` picks the spot; NearestFirst prefers small types, then low floors.
`FeeStrategy` prices a stay; HourlyFee charges per started hour in paise.
Strategies are injected, not singletons, so tests can build any lot.

steps.caption: A car arrives at entry gate IN-1. The gate calls `park` on the lot.
ParkingLot does not search spots itself. It asks the allocation strategy.
NearestFirst tries COMPACT before LARGE, lowest floor first, and returns F1-C1.
The lot creates ticket T-1, marks the spot taken, and the barrier opens.
When the lot is full, the strategy returns nothing and the barrier stays down.
Later the car leaves. ExitGate OUT-1 hands T-1 to the lot.
The lot measures the stay and asks the fee strategy for the amount.
HourlyFee rounds up to whole hours. The spot is freed and the gate opens.

code.title: Facade and strategies
code.caption: The core flow on one thread. Both rules are interfaces passed into the constructor; the concurrency page shows how to claim a spot safely when gates run at once.

walk.text: Two floors, three spots, and one implementation of each strategy.
Four arrivals: two cars, a truck, then a car that finds the lot full.
T-1 leaves after 150 minutes; the waiting car then gets its spot.
Two interfaces are the swap points: where to park, and what to charge.
NearestFirst loops over fitting types first, then floors, then spots.
HourlyFee rounds minutes up to started hours with integer math.
`park` asks the strategy and issues a ticket; `checkout` prices the stay and frees the spot.

code.title: A new strategy
code.caption: A new allocation rule that spreads cars across floors. It is a new class with the same interface; NearestFirst and ParkingLot are not edited.

walk.text: Floor 1 has three of four spots taken, floor 2 one, floor 3 none.
Ask both strategies for a spot for the same car.
The interface is the CoreParking one, vehicle type included.
The existing rule, unchanged: smallest fitting type, then the lowest floor.
Picks the floor with most free fitting spots, ties going lower, then reuses NearestFirst there.

pitfalls: Do not make ParkingLot a static singleton; inject it so tests build fresh lots.
Avoid `if (truck)` branches in the facade; put each rule in a strategy class.
Round started hours up with integer math, never with double division.

quiz.q: What does CoreParking print for the second car?
options: IN-1 KA05CD5678: LOT_FULL, barrier stays down
quiz.why: NearestFirst loops over fitting spot types before floors. COMPACT comes before LARGE, so floor 2's compact spot beats floor 1's large spot.

takeaway: One facade for the gates; every changing rule behind an injected strategy.

starters: Is it wasteful to park a motorbike in a LARGE spot?
Should ParkingLot be a singleton in a real system?
How would I add a weekend flat fee without touching HourlyFee?
